title: Independent check of the twelve zodiac centres: one freestanding Voynich label (f70v2), eleven centres with only the Latin-script word and the ring text
statement: I looked at all twelve inner disks on the Yale scans myself, at 800 by 800 canvas pixels or better, marking everything written inside each disk and, separately, the ring of text around it. Seven of the twelve I had already described blind for the picture steps before reading this step (f70v2, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r and f73v as submitted annotations, f72r3 as an unsubmitted draft); the other five (f70v1, f71r, f71v, f72r1, f72r2) I looked at for this step, knowing its claim. Per centre, emblem as drawn, then writing inside the disk. f70v2, two fish: a Latin-script word between the fish; one Voynich word standing free to the right of the upper star, which is tethered to the upper fish; a second star below with no label. f70v1, a horned animal with a dark green wash eating from a green bush: a Latin-script word under the belly; nothing in Voynich script inside the disk, and no text ring hugging this disk. f71r, a pale horned animal eating a green plant: a Latin-script word on the body; a Voynich text ring around the disk; no freestanding Voynich word. f71v, a pale red horned animal at a basket of green: Latin-script word under the belly; text ring; none freestanding. f72r1, a dark red horned animal at a basket of green: the same arrangement; none freestanding. f72r2, a man in green and a woman in blue clasping hands: Latin-script word between them at knee height; text ring; none freestanding. f72r3, two crayfish-like animals: Latin-script word under the lower one; text ring; none freestanding. f72v3, a four-legged animal with a curled tail: Latin-script word beneath; text ring; none freestanding. f72v2, a clothed figure holding a star: Latin-script word beside the figure; text ring; the star inside the disk has no label. f72v1, a balance: Latin-script word beneath; text ring; none freestanding. f73r, a dark green animal with a looped tail and a tethered star above it: Latin-script word beneath, touching the text ring; the star has no label. f73v, a clothed figure with a crossbow: Latin-script word at the feet, close to the text ring; none freestanding. Result: I find the same single freestanding Voynich string as the step, on f70v2, beside the upper star and separated from the Latin-script word by the upper fish, with no line joining the two. Two things the step does not say and the scans show: the other two centre stars (the lower one on f70v2 and the one on f73r) and the star held on f72v2 carry no label at all, so the f70v2 label looks like an ordinary star label that happens to sit inside the disk, not a caption for the emblem; and on f70v1 the disk has no text ring of its own, so there the Latin-script word is the only writing near the emblem. I did not read or compare the spellings of the Latin-script words and take no view on their date or language. Limits: I knew the step's claim for five of the twelve; and where the Latin-script word touches the ring text (f73r, f73v) I judged by eye that no ring word is set apart for it, which a second reviewer could dispute.
check: Canvases under https://collections.library.yale.edu/iiif/2/ : 1006200 (f70v2), 1006201 (f70v1), 1006202 (f71r), 1006203 (f71v, f72r1, f72r2, f72r3 left to right), 1006204 (f72v3 left, f72v2 right), 1006205 (f72v1), 1006206 (f73r), 1006207 (f73v). For each, crop the inner disk at full size and list every piece of writing inside it by script; list the ring text separately. The claim fails if any centre other than f70v2 holds a Voynich word that stands apart from the ring text, or if a drawn line joins a Voynich word to the Latin-script word anywhere. The side observation fails if either of the other centre stars has a label.
